title: HIV Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis in Solid Organ Transplant Recipients: An Overlooked Component of Long-Term Care.
what: Sexual health and HIV prevention remain inconsistently addressed during follow-up after solid organ transplantation. This narrative review examines the potential role of HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) in transplant recipients with ongoing or anticipated HIV exposure.
why: No clinical trials have evaluated PrEP in solid organ transplant recipients, but existing evidence supports individualized consideration.
pkpd_hook: Tenofovir alafenamide/emtricitabine offers a more favorable renal profile, while long-acting cabotegravir avoids tenofovir exposure.
original_title: HIV Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis in Solid Organ Transplant Recipients: An Overlooked Component of Long-Term Care.
headline: HIV Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis in Solid Organ Transplant Recipients

title: Hepatocyte-based models for cytochrome P450 fraction metabolized determination: Recommendations from the Quantitative Fraction Metabolized Working Group of the International Consortium for Innovation and Quality in Pharmaceutical Development.
what: Accurate quantification of fraction metabolized (fm) by drug metabolizing enzymes is essential for understanding clearance mechanisms, predicting interindividual variability, and assessing victim drug-drug interaction (DDI) risk during drug discovery and development. Particularly, determining fm for metabolically stable, low turnover compounds remains challenging.
why: Study highlights differences in intrinsic clearance, inhibitor response, and fraction metabolized predictions across hepatocyte systems.
pkpd_hook: Differences in metabolite representation, inhibitor behavior, and effective inhibitor exposure may influence fm predictions.
source: PubMed, Drug metabolism and disposition: the biological fate of chemicals
